intended_object: Given i : H ⟶ G between group-valued functors, take a natural transformation f : G → K into a type-valued functor K that is constant on the left cosets of i(H(X)) in G(X) for every X. The intended object is the natural transformation G/i(H) → K that f induces, by the universal property of the pointwise left-coset functor. Inferred from the docstring and the lemma `cosetMk_comp_cosetLift` that follows it.
explanation:
The coset functor `coset i` sends each X to `G.obj X ⧸ (i.app X).hom.range`, which is the quotient by `QuotientGroup.leftRel` of that range. For each X, `cosetLift` takes `Quotient.liftOn'` of `f.app X`, which is well defined by the hypothesis `hf`. Naturality follows from the naturality of `f`, checked on representatives. This is exactly the factorization of f through the pointwise quotient map `cosetMk`. The library proves `cosetMk i ≫ cosetLift i f hf = f`, and `coset_hom_ext` gives uniqueness.

The hypotheses are the right ones: f only has to be constant on the left-coset classes, and K is an arbitrary type-valued functor. The construction depends on the library's own `coset` functor of group-valued functors, so it has no more general Mathlib counterpart. Mathlib's `QuotientGroup.lift` needs a normal subgroup and a group-homomorphism target, so it is a different construction. Nothing in the definition is narrower than its setting requires.
